{% raw %}
What a person can see and do about their own account. [How it is used](../account-api.html).

The user portal's API: everything a person can see and do about their own account in this trust realm. The person is ALWAYS the access token's subject — no operation takes a username, an id or a DN naming whose account it is. A token is obtained by the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) as the public client `sts-user-portal`, with `resource` set to this API, and is DPoP-bound (RFC 9449): send it as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a `DPoP` proof carrying `ath`. It stops working when the sign-on session it was issued on ends. The few operations marked `x-access: link` take no token: they spend the single-use secret of an activation or reset link they carry.

Every answer is checked against the model shown here before it is sent, and no answer carries a member its model does not list. A member shown as *any JSON* is one whose shape belongs to somebody else, and says whose. `.{key}` is a key that is data, and `[]` an element of a list.

## POST /account-api/access-requests

`decideAccessRequest`

**Approves or denies an AuthZEN access request**

Decides one request as you, after the access-control policy (action approve-access-request on resource authzen-access-request) said you may: an approval is handed to the PEP to carry on its next evaluation, which the realm's policy decides afresh; a denial ends the request. Refused for a request you may not decide, your own included where the policy forbids self-approval, and for one no longer pending.

## GET /account-api/activation

`getActivation`

**Checks an activation link and answers the setup form**

Takes no token: the link's `user` and `token` are the credential. Spends nothing — a link opened by a prefetch or a mail scanner still works. Rate limited. Every failure answers the same sentence. The answer is the first step: the password rules, whether a passkey and an authenticator app are offered, and whether a passkey may be the only way in (`passkeyAlone`, #1135).

## POST /account-api/activation

`activate`

**Answers one step of an activation**

`setup` sets the password and starts a passkey (the `key` view) or an authenticator app (the `totp` view) where they were chosen; `key` answers the passkey's ceremony; `totp` the app's code. The link is checked again, claimed before anything is set, and spent only by the step that finishes, which answers the `ready` view. Nobody is signed in by it. A passkey carries no role (#1135): `passkey` asks for one, and `key_role` is still accepted, `primary` and `mfa` both asking for one.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/activate`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string |  | `totp`: the code the authenticator app shows. |
| `confirm` | string |  | `setup`: the password again. |
| `credential` | string |  | `key`: the browser's ceremony result, as JSON. |
| `enrolment_id` | ``, or string |  | `key`: the pending registration. |
| `key_role` | ``, or one of `none`, `primary`, `mfa` |  | Before #1135: `primary` or `mfa` registers a passkey, `none` does not; `passkey` says the same. |
| `kind` | ``, or one of `passkey`, `security-key` |  | `setup`: where the passkey lives. |
| `lane` | ``, or one of `classical`, `pqc` |  | `setup`: `classical` (the default) or `pqc`, where the realm offers a post-quantum passkey beside a classical one. |
| `passkey` | ``, or one of `0`, `1`, `true`, `false`, `on`, `off`, `yes`, `no` |  | `setup`: `1` registers a passkey. |
| `password` | string |  | `setup`: the password to set. |
| `step` | ``, or one of `setup`, `key`, `totp` |  | Which step this answers. |
| `token` | ``, or string |  | The link's single-use token. |
| `totp` | ``, or one of `0`, `1`, `true`, `false`, `on`, `off`, `yes`, `no` |  | `1`: set up an authenticator app too. |
| `user` | ``, or string |  | The username the link names. |

## GET /account-api/announcements

`getAnnouncements`

**Announcements for everybody signed in to the portal**

What an administrator broadcast to the user portal after `since` — the `now` this operation answered your tab's first ask with — within `ssf.announcementKeepS`, oldest first. With no `since` it answers only `now`, so a tab shows what arrived after it signed in. `everyMs` is how often to ask again.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `since` | query | string |  |  |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**200**: The answer.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `announcements` | list |  |  |
| `announcements[].at` | string |  |  |
| `announcements[].id` | string |  |  |
| `announcements[].message` | string |  |  |
| `everyMs` | number |  |  |
| `now` | number |  |  |

**400**: The request did not validate, or was refused: `{ ok: false, errors: [...] }`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

**401**: No access token, or one that does not verify, has expired, was revoked, outlived its sign-on session, or came without its DPoP proof. `WWW-Authenticate` says which.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

**403**: The token is for another audience or does not carry `account:manage`, or the access policy refused the person.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

## POST /account-api/app-passwords

`changeAppPasswords`

**Makes or revokes one of your app passwords**

`create` (rate limited) makes one for the doors whose `door_<id>` is on; the password is in the answer's `view.fresh`, ONCE. `revoke` ends the one `id` names; an id that is not yours is answered as not found.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/app-passwords`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |

## GET /account-api/applications

`getApplications`

**The applications you can be signed in to**

Every registered application that is a sign-in destination (OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0, SAML 1.1, WS-Federation) for which the issuance policy, asked as a dry run, permits you at least one family — its home page, the identity-provider-initiated sign-in links it offers (`launches`, each /launch/{app}?protocol=…), the families permitted and withheld. ## POST /account-api/attributes

## POST /account-api/certificates

`changeCertificates`

**Makes or deletes an enrollment credential, or revokes a certificate**

`create-eab` and `create-challenge` (rate limited) make an ACME account binding key or a SCEP challenge password for your entry; its secret is in the answer's `view.fresh`, ONCE. `delete-eab` and `delete-challenge` remove an unused one of yours; `revoke` revokes a certificate issued for you. Anything that is not yours is answered as not found.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/certificates`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## GET /account-api/ciba

`getSignInRequests`

**The sign-in requests waiting for you, and your user code**

The CIBA requests a client made to sign you in elsewhere (each with its binding message, scopes, requested acr values and expiry), whether you have a CIBA user code, and the GNAP grants waiting for you as their owner — each right with `field` (the checkbox value) and `limitsHtml` (its limit controls). With `stepup` or `gnapstepup` the answer is only `stepUp`: sign in again with `acrValues`, `prompt=login`.

The door of the portal's `GET /portal/ciba`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stepup` | query | string |  | A CIBA request id: answered `stepUp`, the sign-in again its acr values need. |
| `gnapstepup` | query | string |  | A waiting GNAP request id: answered `stepUp`, the sign-in again its rights need. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**200**: The answer.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean |  |  |
| `gnap` | list |  |  |
| `gnap[].acr` | list |  |  |
| `gnap[].acr[]` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].client` | string, or null |  |  |
| `gnap[].declared` | boolean |  |  |
| `gnap[].display` | string, or null |  |  |
| `gnap[].expiresAt` | string or number, or null |  |  |
| `gnap[].id` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].requestedBy` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].rights` | list |  |  |
| `gnap[].rights[].field` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].rights[].limitsHtml` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].rights[].parts` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].rights[].reference` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].rights[].type` | string |  |  |
| `gnap[].subject` | boolean |  |  |
| `hasCode` | boolean |  |  |
| `requests` | list |  |  |
| `requests[].acrValues` | list |  |  |
| `requests[].acrValues[]` | string |  |  |
| `requests[].bindingMessage` | string |  |  |
| `requests[].clientName` | string, or null |  |  |
| `requests[].expiresAt` | string or number, or null |  |  |
| `requests[].id` | string |  |  |
| `requests[].requestContext` | list |  |  |
| `requests[].requestContext[].name` | string |  |  |
| `requests[].requestContext[].value` | string |  |  |
| `requests[].scope` | string, or null |  |  |
| `stepUp` | object |  |  |
| `stepUp.acrValues` | string |  |  |
| `stepUp.maxAge` | number |  |  |
| `stepUp.prompt` | string |  |  |

**400**: The request did not validate, or was refused: `{ ok: false, errors: [...] }`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

**401**: No access token, or one that does not verify, has expired, was revoked, outlived its sign-on session, or came without its DPoP proof. `WWW-Authenticate` says which.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |

## POST /account-api/ciba

`answerSignInRequest`

**Sets your user code, or answers a request**

A JSON body: `action` — `set-code` (with `code`), `clear-code`, `approve` / `deny` (with the CIBA request's `id`), or `gnap-approve` / `gnap-deny` (with the GNAP request's `id`, the ticked `right` values, `subject: "yes"`, and any `lim_t<k>r<r>_<member>` limit controls lowered). An approval stronger than the sign-on session proved is refused 403 with `stepUp`.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/ciba`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | one of `set-code`, `clear-code`, `approve`, `deny`, `gnap-approve`, `gnap-deny` | yes |  |
| `code` | string |  | Your user code. |
| `id` | string |  | The request's id. |
| `right` | list, or string |  |  |
| `right[]` | string |  |  |
| `subject` | one of `yes` |  | Release your identity (GNAP). |

**200**: The answer.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `go` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |

| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

**401**: No access token, or one that does not verify, has expired, was revoked, outlived its sign-on session, or came without its DPoP proof. `WWW-Authenticate` says which.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |

## GET /account-api/claim-sources

`getClaimSources`

**The Claims Providers you can link, and your links**

`providers`: one page (`paging`, moved by `page`) of the Claims Providers this realm registered — each one's id, name, issuer, the claims it supplies and whether they are aggregated or distributed — with your `link` (when, and whether it has gone `stale`) or null. `linked` counts your links over every page. `done` and `problem`, which the provider's callback sends back, come back as `notice` and `problem`.

The door of the portal's `GET /portal/claim-sources`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `problem` | query | string |  | Why a link could not be finished, from the callback. |

## POST /account-api/claim-sources

`linkClaimSource`

**Links or unlinks a Claims Provider**

`link` answers `location`, the provider's authorization endpoint (code flow with PKCE): send the browser there. The answer sets the `sts_claim_link` cookie, scoped to /portal/claim-sources/callback, which finishes the link only in the browser holding it, while the sign-on session this token was issued on is live. `unlink` removes the link.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/claim-sources`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | one of `link`, `unlink` | yes | `link` starts the provider's sign-in; `unlink` removes the link. |
| `id` | string | yes | The Claims Provider's id. |

**200**: The answer.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `go` | string |  |  |
| `location` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

## POST /account-api/connected-accounts

`connectAccount`

**Connects or disconnects a consumer provider**

`connect` answers `location`, the provider's authorization address: send the browser there. It needs a sign-on session whose risk is LOW or unscored, and an authentication within federation.connectRecentAuthMinutes — otherwise the answer is `stepUp`, a sign-in again. ## GET /account-api/credentials/offerable

`getOfferableCredentials`

**The credentials you can put into your own wallet**

`configurations`: each credential configuration this realm's OpenID4VCI issuer offers — its `credential_configuration_id` (`id`), its format, the name its metadata gives it, and whether it names the issuer by DID. `modes`: the two pre-authorized offers, `cross-device` (Appendix H.2) and `deferred` (H.3). `lifetimeSeconds`: how long an offer and its code are honoured (`oid4vci.offerTtlS`). `wallet`: the configured web wallet a link opens, or empty. `batchSize`: how many copies of a credential one issuance gives your wallet, each bound to a different key of the wallet's (`oid4vci.batchSize`, OpenID4VCI 1.0 section 8.2). `issued`: the credentials this realm still records as issued to you, ONE PER ISSUANCE, newest first — each one's `id`, configuration, when it was issued and expires, its `status` (`valid`, `suspended`, `revoked`, `removed` by you, `signed-out` by a global sign-out, `expired`, or `mixed` where its copies differ, with `counts`), whether you can remove it, the last event your wallet reported to the Notification Endpoint (OpenID4VCI 1.0 section 11), and its `copies`: each one's own `id`, `position` of `of`, state, the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the wallet key it is bound to (`keyThumbprint`), the holder's DID where it is DID-bound, and its `statusIndex`. `issued` is one page of issuances (`paging`, moved by `page`, 20 to a page); `paging.total` counts them all. A token whose `sub` and person do not name each other is refused (STS-PORTAL-0617) rather than shown somebody else's history, or nobody's as an empty one.

The door of the portal's `GET /portal/wallet`.

## POST /account-api/credentials/offers

`createCredentialOffer`

**Makes a Credential Offer for your own wallet**

A pre-authorized Credential Offer (OpenID4VCI section 4.1, Appendix H.2 or H.3) of one configuration, about YOU — the token's person; nobody else can be named. Answered once, in place: `offer.credentialOffer`, the offer by value (`offer.byValue.offerUri`, an `openid-credential-offer://` URI, and `walletUrl`, the configured web wallet's link) and by reference (`offer.byReference`, whose `offerUri` is short enough for a QR code, e.g. `openid-credential-offer://?credential_offer_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fsts.example%2Foid4vci%2Fcredential-offer%2F3q2-7w...`), when the offer and its code stop being honoured (`expiresAt`), and the Transaction Code (`txCode`, e.g. `40317`) the wallet will ask for — shown to you, never carried in the offer. The offer is made on the sign-on session your token was issued on, which is reported over CAEP as session-presented (OpenID4VCI). The same `offer` is in `view`, for the page. `signingAlg`, optional, is the algorithm the credential is signed with — one of the configuration's `signingAlgs` in the GET, the post-quantum ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and composite drafts among them for the JOSE formats; left out, the configured default.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/wallet`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `configuration` | string | yes | The `credential_configuration_id` to offer, one of `GET /account-api/credentials/offerable`'s. |
| `mode` | one of `cross-device`, `deferred` | yes | `cross-device` (Appendix H.2: issued as soon as the wallet asks) or `deferred` (H.3: the credential endpoint answers a `transaction_id` first). |
| `page` | ``, or integer |  | Which page of `issued`, newest first. Clamped to the last. |

## POST /account-api/credentials/remove

`removeIssuedCredential`

**Removes a credential issued to you: every copy, or one**

The credential named by its `id` is revoked. An issuance's `id` (from `issued`) names every copy of it — with batch issuance one issuance gives your wallet several copies, each bound to a different key — and removes each copy still good; a copy's `id` (from that issuance's `copies`) removes that copy alone and leaves the others as they are. Each copy removed has its Token Status List entry set INVALID, which is final and what a verifier reads, is marked revoked in the issued register and no longer signs you in; your relying parties are told once over CAEP (credential-change, revoke). It is NOT deleted from your wallet: neither OpenID4VP nor OpenID4VCI lets an issuer do that, so delete it in the wallet yourself. Only a credential of yours can be named; removing one already removed is answered as done. `scope` says what the id named and `removed` how many copies this act removed; the page's `view` is in the answer.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/remove-wallet-credential`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | An issuance's `id`, from `issued` in `GET /account-api/credentials/offerable`, which removes every copy of it; or one copy's, from its `copies`, which removes that copy alone. |
| `page` | ``, or integer |  | Which page of `issued`, newest first. Clamped to the last. |

## GET /account-api/delegate/candidates

`findDelegateCandidates`

**Finds people you may name, by part of their username**

The people of this realm whose username (`uid`, the RDN value of their entry) contains `q`, at least three characters: native people only — never one a federation partner's or a consumer provider's sign-in created — and never you, a disabled account, a service account, a group or an application. ## GET /account-api/devices

`getDevices`

**Your devices, and how to register one**

Each device you own: its applications, whether its Native SSO secret is live, its keys and their attestation, how it was registered and when it was last used. Then the key-proof step (`proof`: the challenge held, with the `audience` and `proofTyp` a proof names), the passkeys built into a device that can be linked (`link`) or the link ceremony armed (`linking`), and whether this browser may be remembered.

## POST /account-api/devices

`actOnDevices`

**Registers, links, remembers or removes a device**

`challenge` then `prove` registers a device by a key proof (or an App Attest object); `link-begin` then `link-finish` links a passkey built into it by a fresh assertion; `remember-browser` remembers this browser (a cookie on the answer); `remove` removes a device and its Native SSO secret. A refusal carries the page's `view`.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/devices`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | ``, or one of `remove`, `challenge`, `prove`, `cancel-proof`, `link-begin`, `link-finish`, `link-cancel`, `remember-browser` |  | What to do; `remove` where none is named. |
| `app_attest_key_id` | string |  | `prove`: an App Attest key id, beside its object. |
| `app_attest_object` | string |  | `prove`: an App Attest attestation object. |
| `challenge` | string |  | `prove`, `link-finish`: the challenge being answered. |
| `credential` | string |  | `link-finish`: the WebAuthn assertion, as JSON. |
| `credential_id` | string |  | `link-begin`: the passkey (built into this device) to link. |
| `device` | string |  | `prove`, `link-begin`: an existing device to add the key to; a new device where empty. |
| `id` | string |  | `remove`: the device. |
| `key_label` | string |  | `prove`: the key's name. |
| `label` | string |  | The device's name. |
| `model` | string |  | The device's model. |
| `os` | string |  | The device's operating system. |
| `platform` | string |  | The device's platform. |
| `proof` | string |  | `prove`: the device-key-proof+jwt JWS. |

|---|---|---|---|

## POST /account-api/devices/challenge

`deviceChallenge`

**A key-proof challenge, for a device app**

Issues a challenge bound to the sign-on session this token was issued on: `{ ok, challenge, audience, typ, expires_at, proof_endpoint }`. The device signs a JWS of type `typ` over `{ nonce: challenge, aud: audience, iat }` with the key it registers, and posts it to `proof_endpoint`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `purpose` | one of `key` |  | What the challenge is for; `key`, the only one. |

| `challenge` | string |  |  |

| `proof_endpoint` | string |  |  |
| `typ` | string |  |  |

## POST /account-api/gnap

## POST /account-api/kerberos

## POST /account-api/keys

`enrolKey`

**Begins, finishes or cancels adding a passkey**

`begin` mints a challenge and holds it (the policy and the `lane`, #643, checked at the door; `algorithms: classical`, #944, the classical retry, refused where the realm forbids a classical passkey); `finish` verifies the browser's registration with the sign-in screen's address rules and answers `go` naming the new passkey; `cancel` drops the waiting one. A refusal carries the page's `view`, except a browser error reported with its own `capabilities` property while the classical retry is offered (#961): that enrolment stays and the answer carries no view. `role` is accepted and ignored since #1135: a passkey carries no role, and the realm decides how every key may be used. `enrol.allowed` says whether the realm accepts a new passkey for any use.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/keys`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | ``, or one of `begin`, `finish`, `cancel` |  | `begin` mints a challenge, `finish` answers it, `cancel` drops it. |
| `algorithms` | ``, or one of `classical` |  | `begin`: `classical` retries with the classical algorithms only, where `enrol.pending.fallback.classical` says the realm allows it. |
| `credential` | string |  | `finish`: the browser's ceremony result, as JSON. |
| `enrolment_id` | ``, or string |  | `finish`: the pending enrolment the ceremony answers. |
| `kind` | ``, or one of `passkey`, `security-key` |  | `begin`: which call to action was pressed. |
| `lane` | ``, or one of `classical`, `pqc` |  | `begin`: `classical` (the default) or `pqc`, where the realm offers a post-quantum passkey beside a classical one. |
| `role` | ``, or one of `primary`, `mfa` |  | Ignored since #1135: a passkey carries no role. |

**200**: The answer.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `go` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean |  |  |

## POST /account-api/keys/remove

`removeKey`

**Removes one of your passkeys**

Refused where it would leave you no way to sign in. Your relying parties are told over CAEP, and every session the passkey signed in ends (`sessionsEnded` counts them, #722); your other sessions stay.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/remove-key`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

## POST /account-api/language

`setLanguage`

**Sets or removes your preferred language**

Writes `preferredLanguage` on your own entry (RFC 2798), which ranks above the browser for every page this service draws for you, and sets the language cookie; an empty `lang` removes it and follows the browser. A tag no catalog answers is refused.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/language`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

## POST /account-api/mfa

`changeMfa`

**Sets up, confirms or removes your second factors**

`start` mints a secret and holds it (ask the view for the QR code); `confirm` checks a code from the app (rate limited) and enrols it; `remove` takes it off, and ends every session its codes signed in (`sessionsEnded`, #722). `generate-codes` answers a set of recovery codes ONCE, in `view.fresh`, and stores nothing; `confirm-codes` stores their hashes; `discard-codes` throws the pending set away. `email-factor-on` (with `kind`) and `email-factor-off` opt in and out of the emailed second factor. A refusal carries the page's `view`.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/mfa`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |

| `code` | string |  | For `confirm`: the code the app shows. |
| `handle` | string |  | For `confirm-codes` and `discard-codes`: the pending set's handle, from `generate-codes`'s answer. |

## GET /account-api/overview

`getOverview`

**Who you are, this session, and how you sign in**

Your username, subject and directory entry's DN; when the sign-on session began, how it authenticated (amr, acr) and when it ends; every standard inetOrgPerson attribute your entry holds, from a fixed list (`directory`, null with no directory or no entry — then `session` carries what the sign-in said); a summary of your credentials (`mechanisms`); the language your entry holds with those offered (`language`); and the realm's custom attributes whose definition shows them on the portal, with your values and whether you may change them (`customAttributes`, empty with no entry).

## POST /account-api/password

`changePassword`

**Changes your password**

Re-proves the current password (rate limited, in the budget the Kerberos keytab shares), screens the new one against breached passwords, applies the password policy, and tells your relying parties over CAEP. A refusal carries the page's `view`.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/password`.

## POST /account-api/reset-password

`spendPasswordReset`

## GET /account-api/self-issued

`getSelfIssued`

**The wallet keys that sign you in with SIOPv2**

`subjects`: each enrolled self-issued subject (a DID or a JWK thumbprint), its label, when and by whom it was enrolled, and how (`proof`: `wallet`, proved by you, or `admin`, by an administrator), whether it is your preferred DID (`preferred`, #693), and where the key came from (`location`: `{ kind, value }` — `web`, the web wallet at that address; `app`, a wallet app, by the name it reported or ''; `dc_api`, your browser, by its origin or ''; `admin`; or null, not recorded), and where its DID document is (`didDocumentUrl`, a did:web's published address, or `didResolved`, a did:jwk or did:key resolved from the identifier at /portal/self-issued/did). `enabled`: whether the self-issued sign-in is on; `turnOn`, where it is off: the setting (`setting`) and environment variable (`env`) that turn it on, whether you may change it (`administrator`: you hold Admin Write in this realm) and, if you may, the console page that does (`page`); null where it is on. `didClaim`: whether the preferred DID may be released as the `did` claim here. A key is enrolled by proving it, at /authn/wallet?siop=1&amp;enrol=1, which comes back with `enrolled=1`; `notice` then says so. Where the directory holds no entry for the person the token names it is refused (STS-PORTAL-0616) rather than answered as an empty list. `published` (#1291): whether this realm publishes a did:web for you (`enabled`), who holds its key (`custody`: `wallet`, `realm` or `download`), how many you may hold (`maxPerPerson`) and hold now (`active`), whether you may publish one more (`canPublish`), and each one you hold (`dids`): its `rid`, `did`, `documentUrl`, `custody`, `state` (`active`, `deactivated`), `proof`, `preferred`, `currentVersion`, any change waiting for its new key (`pending`) and its `versions`, each with its keys and what authorized it. A wallet act that just finished comes back with `did` (`published`, `authorized` or `changed`), and `notice` says so.

The door of the portal's `GET /portal/self-issued`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enrolled` | query |  |  | `1` when the wallet sign-in has just enrolled a subject. |
| `did` | query |  |  | A published DID's wallet act that has just finished (#1291): `published`, `authorized` (the change's first proof; prove the new key next) or `changed`. |
| `rid` | query |  |  | The published DID that act was about. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

|---|---|---|---|

## POST /account-api/self-issued

`removeSelfIssued`

**Removes a self-issued subject of yours, or marks one as your preferred DID**

`remove` (the default): the subject no longer signs you in. One that is not enrolled for you is refused. `prefer` (#693): marks one DID you PROVED with your wallet as your preferred one — the one a client you consent to may be told as the `did` claim, where the realm releases it (`oauth2.didClaim`); a subject an administrator added, or a JWK thumbprint, is refused (STS-PORTAL-0615). `unprefer` clears the mark. Removing the preferred subject clears it too.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/self-issued`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

## GET /account-api/self-issued/did

`getSelfIssuedDidDocument`

**The DID document of one of your enrolled did:jwk or did:key subjects**

`document`: the DID document of `subject`, resolved from the identifier itself — a did:jwk or did:key is its own document, so nothing is published and nothing is fetched. Only a subject enrolled for you: any other is refused (STS-PORTAL-0618), and a did:web (its document is the one published at its address, linked from the list) or a JWK thumbprint (no DID) is refused (STS-PORTAL-0619). With no `subject`, `{ subject: '', document: null }`.

The door of the portal's `GET /portal/self-issued/did`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `subject` | query |  |  | One of your enrolled self-issued subjects: a did:jwk or a did:key. Left out, the page says to choose one. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**200**: The answer.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | any JSON |  | A DID document as the DID's method resolved it (W3C DID Core), or null: its verification methods and services are the DID controller's to state. A DID document as the DID's method resolved it (W3C DID Core), or null: its verification methods and services are the DID controller's to state. |

| `subject` | string |  |  |

## POST /account-api/self-issued/dids

`actOnPublishedDid`

**Publishes a did:web for you, changes its key, or deactivates it**

A did:web this realm publishes for you (#1291), where it does (`did.personPublishing`). `publish`: a new DID whose key this realm generates — kept sealed in `realm` custody, or answered ONCE as `view.fresh.file` (a private JWK) in `download` custody and never kept. In `wallet` custody a DID is published, and its key changed, by proving keys with your wallet at /authn/wallet?siop=1&amp;enrol=1&amp;did_act=…, and this act refuses those (STS-VC-0173). `add-key` and `rotate-key` of a `realm`-custody DID append a version with a newly generated key, beside or instead of the current ones. `deactivate` ends one: its address answers 410 Gone for good, its history stays resolvable, and it no longer signs you in, nor is it preferred or released. Refusals carry the library's code (STS-VC-0167 to STS-VC-0176).

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/self-issued/dids`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | one of `publish`, `add-key`, `rotate-key`, `deactivate` | yes | `publish` a DID whose key this realm generates (`realm` or `download` custody); `add-key` or `rotate-key` of a `realm`-custody DID; `deactivate` one of your DIDs. |
| `rid` | ``, or string |  | The published DID's random id, from the list; every action but `publish` names one. |

## GET /account-api/shared

`getShared`

**What you share through User-Managed Access**

One page (`paging`) of `resources`: the resources resource servers registered on your behalf, each with its scopes and the `shares` your sharing policy holds for it; the `custom` rules of your policy the share form did not write, with their ALFA; the `pending` requests waiting for your approval; and, where the realm allows it (`alfaEditing`), your whole policy as `alfa`. `enabled` says whether UMA is on.

The door of the portal's `GET /portal/shared`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

## POST /account-api/shared

`actShared`

**Shares a resource, removes a share, or rewrites your policy**

`action` share writes one rule into your sharing policy: a resource of yours, its scopes, and who — a person, a group, anyone signed in to this realm, or anyone whose claim has a value — with an optional expiry, authentication level and "ask me each time". `approve` and `refuse` answer a request waiting for you; an approval adds a share for that person for a day. `unshare` removes one and revokes the requesting party tokens that carried it. `alfa` replaces the whole policy, where the realm allows it, and revokes every token over your resources. A resource or share that is not yours is refused.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/shared`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acr` | ``, or string |  | share: an optional authentication level the requesting party's session must meet. |
| `action` | one of `share`, `unshare`, `alfa`, `approve`, `refuse` | yes | share adds a share; unshare removes one; alfa replaces the whole document, where the realm allows it; approve and refuse answer a request waiting for you. |
| `alfa` | ``, or string |  | alfa: the whole document, as ALFA. |
| `askMe` | ``, or one of `0`, `1`, `true`, `false`, `on`, `off`, `yes`, `no` |  | share: ask the owner each time. |
| `claim` | ``, or string |  | share, recipientKind claim: the claim's name. |
| `expires` | ``, or string |  | share: an optional date the share ends. |
| `page` | ``, or integer |  | The page of the list the form was on. |
| `pending` | ``, or string |  | approve, refuse: the waiting request's id, from the list. |
| `recipient` | ``, or string |  | share: the username, the group's name, or the claim's value. |
| `recipientKind` | ``, or one of `person`, `group`, `realm`, `claim` |  | share: who the share is with. |
| `resource` | ``, or string |  | share: the resource's _id, one of yours. |
| `scope` | list, or ``, or string |  |  |
| `scope[]` | string |  |  |
| `share` | ``, or string |  | unshare: the share's id, from the list. |

## POST /account-api/signing-key

`changeSigningKeys`

**Generates or revokes a signing key or TLS certificate**

`generate` ADDS a key pair for `purpose` from this realm's Issuing CA, named by `label` (refused at the cap); `revoke` revokes one of yours by `handle`, with `reason`: its certificate goes on the CRL and the key stops being accepted. `generate-tls-client` issues a TLS client certificate; `revoke-tls-client` revokes one of yours. Both generations answer the private key (unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM) and the certificate chain ONCE, in `view.fresh.files.key` and `view.fresh.files.chain` (base64). Both generations are refused (403) where self-service is off, and rate limited. A refusal carries the page's `view`.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/signing-key`.

Scope: `account:manage`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | ``, or one of `generate`, `revoke`, `generate-tls-client`, `revoke-tls-client` |  | `generate` a signing key pair (for `purpose`) or `revoke` one of yours (by `handle`); `generate-tls-client` or `revoke-tls-client` a TLS client certificate. |
| `handle` | string |  | For `revoke`: the key pair's `kid` (RFC 7523) or certificate thumbprint (RFC 7522), one of yours. |
| `key_alg` | ``, or one of `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `ec-p256`, `ec-p384` |  | For `generate-tls-client`: the key algorithm. |
| `label` | string |  | For `generate`: what you call the key pair. For `generate-tls-client`: what you call the device. |
| `purpose` | ``, or one of `jwt`, `saml` |  | For `generate` and `revoke`: RFC 7523's `jwt` key pairs (the default) or RFC 7522's `saml` ones. |
| `reason` | ``, or one of `cessationOfOperation`, `keyCompromise` |  | For `revoke` and `revoke-tls-client`: why. |
| `serial` | string |  | For `revoke-tls-client`: the certificate's serial, one of yours. |

## GET /account-api/verify-email

`getEmailVerification`

**Checks an address verification link, and spends nothing**

Takes no token: the link's `user` and `token` are the credential. Answers the address the link would verify, or `view.refused`. Opening it spends nothing, so a mail scanner cannot verify an address nobody read. Rate limited.

The door of the portal's `GET /portal/verify-email`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | query |  |  | The username the link names. |
| `X-Link-Token` | header | string |  | The single-use secret the link carried in its fragment. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for the DPoP-bound access token, which `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `X-Requested-With` | header | string |  | Added by an Android WebView, naming the application that hosts the page. This API reads nothing in it. |

**200**: The answer.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
